title: ATune: Heart Rate and Game Sounds in Your Terminal
summary: Colin McNamara uses a chest-strap ECG to learn which alert sounds keep him in flow at the terminal.

chapters.title: Sounds That Land and Sounds That Jar

learn: Being pulled out of flow can cost about 20 minutes, so he built ATune, a Rust app that reads ECG from a Polar H10 heart rate monitor over Bluetooth at 130 Hz alongside his coding terminal.
It windows the ECG around each alert sound and scores whether he oriented back to the task or startled; in his data a Zelda sound calmed him and a Duke Nukem sound did not.
It turns those scores into a reward function and keeps tuning its sound choices: sounds compete in leagues like a bracket, and a recency decay shows that a sound's calming effect fades.
The idea comes from the HarnessX paper on self-improving harnesses, which he heard about in a talk by Esteban Puerta at Antler.
Data stays local, with a Qwen3.5 27B model on his machine doing private digestion and Claude and Codex checking each other; the terminal is herdr, a front end for tmux.
